scope: L0: desk-checked; bench confirmation pending. Marker: `cmdDisp.CMD_NO_OP_STRING(arg1)` -> event `cmdDisp.NoOpStringReceived`, the id sent as a decimal string. Link budget [I]: RFM69 at the catalog default data rate 19200 bit/s carries about 2400 byte/s; sensor telemetry at 1 Hz leaves the rest to CFDP, so a 100 kB product takes on the order of a minute.
- UUT: the PiSensor deployment of `docs/ssdd.md` on the Raspberry Pi 5 `soakee`, 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS.

- Test deployment: the deployment itself. No component is added for testing. Markers use `cmdDisp`, the on-board file check uses `fileManager.CalculateCrc`, the directory listing uses `fileManager.ListDirectory`, product names come from `dpWriter.FileWritten`, platform identity is a bench action over ssh.

- Ground system: fprime-yamcs at the ledger pin with the project YAMCS configuration directory (CFDP service), joined to the RFM69 link by the bench ground radio (bench setup, not part of the SSDD; it passes TM and TC frames unchanged and is recorded in the manifest).

- Record content (`record/`): every exported row carries the ground reception time beside the FSW time; `record/raw/bench-actions.log` holds each bench action with its bench start and end time; every CFDP file received is copied to `record/raw/files/` before it is checked; CFDP class and outcome come from the YAMCS transfer record exported to `record/raw/cfdp.json`.

- Completeness: every window requires STD; an overflowed queue or a gap in the downlinked TM frame count makes the window UNVERIFIED, never a pass of an absence or count check. The frame counts come from the YAMCS frame record, exported to `record/raw/frames.json`.
- Bench and Pi clocks: both synchronised by NTP; the offset is measured at L0-1 and must be under 0.5 s; tolerances that compare the two clocks use 2 s.
- Heartbeat: `bmpManager.Reading` (revision 2: the MPU6050 channel gates no window), written to the telemetry packet every 1 Hz cycle; `cmdDisp.CommandsDispatched` updates on change only.
- Minimum sample counts come from the requirement: one sample per 2 s of window outside a downlink (30 in 60 s, 15 in 30 s).

- `dpCat.START_XMIT_CATALOG` is always sent with `remainActive` false: a product stored after the catalog is built is not sent once that downlink has finished. Each test that carries `capture_before_xmit` waits 30 s (the REQ-PiSensor-007 bound) before it builds the catalog, so every product of the test is stored first; L2-8 waits for both `dpWriter.FileWritten` events.
- Telemetry gaps are judged on ground reception time: the requirement is stated at the ground. Telemetry is sent at 1 Hz, so the 2 s bound leaves one period of margin for radio delay.
- CFDP as shipped deletes a file after sending it (`cfdpManager.FileInDefaultKeep`, default DELETE): the on-board CRC is taken before the downlink, and L7-1 sets KEEP.

- Constants: temperature -20 to 60 degC and gravity 8 to 12 m/s^2 are plausibility bounds for an indoor bench at rest; 1 km is the GPS plausibility bound around the surveyed bench position; 0.1 deg is the rounding allowance of the roll and pitch computation; the L2-5 widening values (0.5 degC, 2 deg, 0.0001 deg) are noise allowances for a bench at rest [I], to be confirmed against the BMP280 and MPU6050 datasheets and the receiver accuracy at the bench refresh; `piCamera.CaptureFailed` is the name planned for the capture failure event, confirmed against the `piCamera` SDD at the same refresh; the 30 s downlink precondition is three times the 10 s bound; the file CRC is that of `Os::File::calculateCrc`; the product directory is `DataProductsConfig.Paths.dpDir`.

- Open character devices allowed to the deployment process (device paths of the project configuration): the SPI devices of the RFM69 and the BMP280, the I2C bus of the MPU6050, the GPS UART, the camera devices, `/dev/null`, `/dev/urandom`.
- The 2 in the frame count checks of L2-7 and L2-8 allows one frame in flight at each `PacketsTransmitted` snapshot.

- Commands (revision 2): in every window, the commands sent, marker commands apart, equal the `cmdDisp.OpCodeDispatched` events of opcodes other than the marker's. The dispatch event of a marker carries the time of the marker event and can sort outside the window; a lost marker is judged by the marker precondition. The RFM69 uplink has no retransmission: the bench sender sends a command again, at most twice, when the unit does not report its dispatch within 6 s, and logs each resend in `record/raw/cmd/resend.log`; with r resends logged in the window the dispatch count may lie between the commands sent and that number plus r. A command dispatched twice still fails the count checks of its test.

- Missing sensor data (revision 3, human ruling of 2026-11-20 in `docs/ledger.md`, REQ-PiSensor-005 as amended): a capture stores its product whether or not a sensor answers. Nothing is substituted. A metric marked valid is judged as before (sample time within 2 s, REQ-PiSensor-014; agreement with the telemetry in L2-5). A metric marked not valid passes only as a NaN placeholder with a zero sample time, with the `piCamera` event of that sensor in the window, and with no telemetry sample of that sensor in the record in the 2 s up to the capture time record; a lost TM frame cannot fake that silence, since it makes the window unverified (Completeness). In every window, a `piCamera.TemperatureUnavailable`, `AttitudeUnavailable` or `LocationUnavailable` event is a failure when the record holds a telemetry sample of that sensor in the 2 s up to its capture time (the time in the name of the product written next in the window; the event time where none follows). These events are WARNING_LO and no precondition reads the warning severities.

- GPS without a fix (revision 3): the `gpsManager.Reading` period and plausibility checks are unchanged and fail. They are judged in L2-1 and L2-2 (REQ-PiSensor-003) and in L2-9 (the GPS item of REQ-PiSensor-012, moved there unchanged from window D of L2-7 and L2-8, which keep the BMP280 and MPU6050 items). No other test reads the GPS channel except through a product metric marked valid.
- Telemetry period checks select the samples by ground reception time between the reception times of the two markers.

- Every window ends with a wait, before its END marker, until a `bmpManager.Reading` sample with a unit time of that moment or later has reached the ground (at most 60 s): telemetry reaches the ground one to two seconds after it is sampled, and a window is judged right after its END marker. No bound of a requirement depends on this wait.
- Out of scope: BMP280 pressure; yaw.
entry_gates: - Component campaign `picam` closed; its unit tests pass.
- Image built from the manifest SHAs; L0-1 and L0-2 pass on the bench.
- Product directory empty at the start of each test (bench teardown empties the product directory over ssh; L7-1 has no teardown).

- Frame loss measured over a 5 min downlink at the bench refresh and recorded; if a window of that length is not normally gap-free, the STD frame term is restated on the space-packet sequence counts of the event and telemetry APIDs before the plan is approved.
- Bench recipe: BMP280, MPU6050, GPS receiver with a fix and Pi Camera attached to the Pi 5; RFM69 ground radio joined to fprime-yamcs on the ground host (supplied with the bench).
levels: L0 provenance and feasibility · L2 functional · L7 final state. No L3, L4, L5 or L6 test: no system requirement states restart, endurance, fault or rejection behaviour; those belong to the components.
not_covered: - Fault, warning and rejection behaviour of `piCamera`: its component campaign.
- Fault and warning behaviour of inherited components: not required at system level; their own tests, where they exist, cover it.
- CFDP uplink, packet loss and retransmission: no system requirement.
- Radio interference and range: the RFM69 link is tested at bench range only.
- Bench of 2026-11-19: BMP280, GPS receiver (fix), camera and ground radio answer; the MPU6050 is silent (see Scope).
- Revision 3. REQ-PiSensor-003 has no passing test while the GPS has no fix: L2-1 and L2-2 are its only tests and both fail.
- Revision 3. A silent BMP280 leaves every window unverified: the Heartbeat is `bmpManager.Reading`. The temperature placeholder is then judged by the component campaign only.

- Revision 3. Sensor silence is read from the telemetry. The frame count precondition of a window covers the frames between its markers; the 2 s up to a capture can begin before the START marker (a capture follows it by under 1 s), and a frame lost there is not seen by that window. To show a 1 Hz sensor silent that was answering, two consecutive samples of it would have to be lost; about 1 TM frame in 650 is lost on this link.

- Revision 3. The unit time of a telemetry sample is taken as the time the sensor was read (`Svc.TlmPacketizer` stamps a packet with the last write to one of its channels). Assumed, to be confirmed on the first record with a product.
decision_log: 1. 2026-11-18 designer — test deployment = the deployment as flown; no test component (human direction).
2. 2026-11-18 designer — product content is judged on the ground copy of the file; `fileManager.CalculateCrc` gives the on-board check and the bench `sha256sum` the independent final state.
3. 2026-11-18 designer — planted faults insert commands of existing components only; a grown or altered product file is not usable as a fault because `Svc.DpCatalog` refuses it (size check).
4. 2026-11-18 designer — every test makes its own product; no test depends on a product of another test.

5. 2026-11-19 harness builder, revision 2 — see the changelog in `test/int/README.md`: per-channel telemetry period metrics, Heartbeat on `bmpManager.Reading`, command count with marker commands apart and logged resends, clock action in the L0-1 procedure, IMU bounds stated in the units of the channel, roll and pitch validity as a check of its own.

6. 2026-11-20 harness builder, revision 3 (REQ-PiSensor-005 as amended by the human ruling of 2026-11-20) — see the changelog in `test/int/README.md`: product metrics judged valid or not valid per sensor, the sensor-unavailable event check in every window, the GPS item of REQ-PiSensor-012 in its own test L2-9.
